statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 13 while Stress stays elevated at 48.
recommendation: Tail sits well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The decisive evidence is that Wednesday's gap-down was fully retraced and the index closed within ten points of its session high while VIX decayed from 16.01 to 15.08. Stress remains elevated on 24-year-high long-end yields, Brent above $100 and a narrow, megacap-led tape. The one named caution window is Thursday's 17:00-19:00 UTC block containing the 30-year bond auction and a Fed speaker, where a duration-driven second leg is the main conditional risk.
headline: NDX closes 31,160.08 near its session high after fully retracing the gap-down, with VIX back to 15.08
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 31,160.08, down 64.61 points or 0.21% against Tuesday's 31,224.69 close. The path matters more than the level: the index gapped down to open at 30,976.25, fell to 30,904.46, then recovered the entire decline to print a 31,170.12 session high and settle within ten points of it. A completed retracement of that size, finishing at the top of the range, is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures, which is why Tail eases to 13. Volatility decayed in parallel: VIX closed at 15.08 after a 16.01 session high. The September 15-16 FOMC minutes, released Wednesday, were hawkish, recording a unanimous 12-0 vote for the quarter-point increase to a 3-3/4 to 4 percent target range and most participants judging another increase likely appropriate by year end. Price discovery since has been orderly rather than one-way: the 10-year yield closed near 5.28% after touching 5.36%, its highest since April 2002, and the 30-year closed at 5.66% after a 5.73% print, its highest since May 2002. Stress stays elevated at 48 because that duration stress is unresolved, Brent is trading near and above $100 on Houthi attacks and Strait of Hormuz disruption, and the recovery was narrow: the Russell 2000 fell 1.31% and the Dow 0.66% against a 0.22% decline in the Nasdaq Composite, while bitcoin slid to about $83,000. Those are difficult-environment and drawdown inputs rather than evidence of a pathological price path, so they raise Stress without lifting Tail. Shared Finviz context was present but eight days stale and flagged partial, so it was disregarded and the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. Risk was low and mean-reverting through the late 6 October session and the Asian and early European hours of 7 October, with Tail between 10 and 14. From 11:00 to 14:00 UTC a trend-down phase lifted Tail to a 23 peak and Stress to 54 as long-end yields pushed to multi-decade highs ahead of the 10-year auction. From 15:00 UTC the mode reverted to mixed and Tail eased through 20, 18, 17, 15 and 14 as the gap-down was absorbed and the FOMC minutes landed. Confidence held between 86 and 89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The near-term path is treated as conditionally two-way. Risk eases from the current 13 through the post-close and Asian hours to an 11 floor, since thin but orderly overnight trade normally still permits retracement. Risk then rebuilds across the European morning on duration sensitivity, through the 08:30 UTC Fed Waller speech, the 12:30 UTC jobless-claims release and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where Tail reaches the 19 low-band ceiling. The one named caution block is 17:00-19:00 UTC on 8 October, covering the 30-year bond auction and the 17:40 UTC Fed Musalem speech, where Tail is lifted to 22 and then 20 in the watch band because a weak long-end auction into a 5.66% 30-year is the most credible duration-driven one-way mechanism. Tail returns to 17 in the final hour before the close. Every forecast hour beyond the current one frames price-path structure conditionally; none asserts observed structure.
